Stat. § 47a-21(d) read with § 47a-21(a)(14) ('tenant's obligations'), retrieved verbatim from cga.ct.gov on 2026-06-05: at termination the landlord returns the deposit plus accrued interest, less the value of damages from the tenant's failure to comply with the tenant's obligations (§ 47a-11) — i.e. NOT ordinary wear and tear. Return window: 21 days after termination, or 15 days after a written forwarding address, whichever is later. status=draft-unverified.

rules.title: Automatic deposit deduction for painting / cleaning / ordinary wear
rules.description: Per § 47a-21(d), a landlord may deduct from the deposit only the value of damages caused by the tenant's failure to meet their obligations (plus unpaid rent) — not ordinary wear and tear. A clause auto-deducting for repainting, routine cleaning, or 'normal wear' is suspect; flag it to check the charge reflects actual tenant-caused damage.
rules.tenant_explainer: Your landlord can take money out of your deposit for damage you caused or unpaid rent — not for normal wear and tear, routine repainting, or standard cleaning. Watch for clauses that auto-charge those to your deposit.

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-21(d) — return of deposit; lawful deductions
citations.quote: … shall pay to the tenant … (A) The amount of any security deposit … less the value of any damages … as a result of such tenant's failure to comply with such tenant's obligations; and (B) any accrued interest. … Not later than twenty-one days after termination of a tenancy or fifteen days after receiving written notification of [the tenant's forwarding address], whichever is later.

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-21(a)(14) — 'tenant's obligations' (limits deductions)
citations.quote: 'Tenant's obligations' means (A) the amount of any rental or utility payment due the landlord from a tenant; (B) a tenant's obligations under the provisions of section 47a-11; and (C) the actual reasonable cost of changing the locks … pursuant to section 47a-7b ….
